  <title>EDPB publishes statement on the data protection challenges of smart glasses</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-publishes-statement-on-the-data-protection-challenges-of-smart-glasses_en</link>
  <description>&lt;p&gt;Brussels, 13 October – During its latest plenary, the EDPB has adopted &lt;a href="https://www.edpb.europa.eu/documents/statement/statement-of-the-edpb-on-smart-glasses_en"&gt;statement on smart glasses&lt;/a&gt; and published the &lt;a href="https://www.edpb.europa.eu/documents/support-pool-of-experts/the-connected-gaze-video-recording-surveillance-and-administering_en"&gt;report “The connected gaze. Video recording, surveillance and administering evidence in the age of smart glasses”&lt;/a&gt;*, developed in the context of the &lt;a href="https://www.edpb.europa.eu/support-pool-of-experts-spe-programme_en"&gt;Support Pool of Expert (SPE) programme&lt;/a&gt;**.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As smart glasses become widely available and more frequently used, they raise significant questions for the protection of individuals’ personal data and rights and freedoms even if they create new opportunities for communication, assistance, and innovation.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;“These devices look like ordinary glasses, but they include cameras and microphones and are connected to the internet. This raises serious privacy concerns, as individuals may be recorded without their knowledge.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The risks are even greater in sensitive environments—such as hospitals, schools, or workplaces—and when recordings are shared on social networks. And of course, children are especially at risk when using these glasses or when they are filmed.“&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;EDPB Chair, Anu Talus&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;The EDPB’s text is an initial statement which provides preliminary guidance to users, manufacturers and service providers while increasing awareness about the risks these devices pose.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Shared responsibility&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The user’s responsibility for processing personal data under the GDPR depends on the way they use their smart glasses. For example, if this involves sharing a photo or video on a public social media account, or if smart glasses are used as part of official, professional, or political activities, the &lt;strong&gt;user would be considered a data controller&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;However, if the user shares a photo or records a video of family members or friends, or if they use the device for personal translation purposes in a private context, this would be considered a purely personal activity for which the GDPR would not apply (household exemption). In any case, even when the GDPR does not apply, the use of smart glasses may still be subject to criminal, civil, or labour law - as well as other sector-specific rules.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As data controllers, &lt;strong&gt;neither the producer nor the provider of a linked application or service can transfer their obligations to users&lt;/strong&gt;. They must comply with data protection law and ensure any new data processing remains compatible with the original purpose of collection.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;The importance of transparency&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The EDPB highlights transparency as one of the main data protection challenges posed by smart glasses. Due to their discreet appearance and use, bystanders may be unaware that personal data relating to them is being processed, by whom, and for what purposes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;“Smart glasses should make their recording obvious – for instance with bright LED lights, audio signals or voice activation cues, privacy-friendly smartphone notifications, or unique designs. These warnings need to be reliable, hard to ignore, and always up to date.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Even in public spaces, bystanders should clearly understand that someone is filming or photographing them. Because when it comes to privacy, individuals deserve clear warnings, not hidden surprises.”&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;EDPB Chair, Anu Talus&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Lastly, the statement encourages industry standards and awareness-raising measures to help individuals understand when smart glasses are being used and how their personal data is used.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Expert insights&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The report “The connected gaze. Video recording, surveillance and administering evidence in the age of smart glasses” was commissioned by the Board, through its SPE programme and following a proposal from the French DPA, to better understand smart glasses usage, their privacy implications, and assess their societal acceptability.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The report, developed by a digital sociologist, examines both user experiences with smart glasses and non-users' perceptions of associated risks, supported by real-life examples from interviewees.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The research shows that smart glasses are sometimes becoming instruments of interpersonal surveillance and handling of evidence. Furthermore, individuals’ ability to use these devices effectively varies widely, creating power imbalances between those who use them and those being recorded.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Note to editors:&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span&gt;*This document was not produced by the EDPB. It was prepared by an external contractor as part of the SPE programme. The views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the official position of the EDPB.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span&gt;**The Support Pool of Experts (SPE) is a key initiative of the EDPB, which is part of the&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.edpb.europa.eu/documents/reports-statements-and-letters/edpb-strategy-2024-2027_en" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span&gt;EDPB 2024-2027 Strategy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span&gt;. The main objective of this programme is to help European Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) increase their capacity to supervise and enforce data protection rules by developing common tools and giving them access to a wide pool of experts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>

  <title>Italian DPA fines Wind Tre EUR 16 700 000 for unlawful telemarketing and data protection infringements</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/italian-dpa-fines-wind-tre-eur-16-700-000-for-unlawful-telemarketing-and-data-protection_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 05/06/2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: Wind Tre S.p.A.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 6 (Lawfulness of processing), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject), Article 15 (Right to access by the data subject), Article 21 (Right to object), Article 24 (Responsibility of the controller), Article 25 (Data protection by design and by default) and Article 32 (Security of processing)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine, Definitive ban on data processing, Compliance order&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Website topics: Data subjects rights, Basic principles, Legal basis, Marketing&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case &amp;nbsp;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) carried out an investigation into Wind Tre S.p.A. following numerous complaints and reports from individuals concerning unsolicited promotional contacts and the activation of contracts and services without their knowledge.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The investigation also concerned the effectiveness of the measures adopted by the company to ensure compliance with data protection rules throughout its sales network and to manage data subjects’ requests.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Authority examined, in particular, the processing carried out for telemarketing purposes, the procedures used to conclude contracts through sales partners and the technical and organisational measures implemented by Wind Tre to prevent unlawful processing.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA found several infringements concerning the processing of personal data for marketing and contractual purposes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Individuals continued to receive promotional communications despite having exercised their right to object or without having given valid consent. The investigation also identified cases in which contracts were activated without the individuals’ knowledge, involving the unlawful processing of their personal data.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;They found shortcomings in Wind Tre’s technical and organisational measures and in the controls implemented over its sales network. The company had not ensured that its systems and procedures were capable of effectively preventing unlawful processing and of promptly giving effect to data subjects’ requests.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The DPA also identified infringements concerning the principles of accountability, data protection by design and by default and security of processing.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA imposed an administrative fine of EUR 16 700 000 on Wind Tre S.p.A.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;They also prohibited the further processing of personal data acquired without consent and ordered the company to adopt measures to ensure effective compliance with data subjects’ rights, particularly the right to object to processing for direct marketing purposes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Wind Tre was also required to strengthen the technical and organisational measures governing its sales network and the procedures used to verify the lawfulness of data processing connected with promotional activities and the activation of contracts.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA stressed that controllers &lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10272004#1"&gt;https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10272004#1&lt;/a&gt;using complex sales networks remain responsible for ensuring that personal data are processed in compliance with the GDPR and must implement effective technical and organisational measures to prevent unlawful marketing activities and unauthorised contractual activations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10272004#1"&gt;Data breach, il Garante privacy sanziona Wind Tre per 1,7 milioni di euro&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>

  <title>Italian DPA fines IQVIA EUR 7 000 000 for unlawful processing of patients’ health data</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/italian-dpa-fines-iqvia-eur-7-000-000-for-unlawful-processing-of-patients-health-data_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 23 September 2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: IQVIA Solutions Italy S.r.l&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 9 (Processing of special categories of personal data), &amp;nbsp;Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject), Article 25 (Data protection by design and by default), Article 28 (Processor) and Article 35 (Data protection impact assessment)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Key words: Data protection impact assessment, Health and research, Anonymisation/pseudonymisation, Privacy by design and by default, Fines, Basic principles and Controller/processor&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) carried out an investigation into IQVIA Solutions Italy S.r.l., a company belonging to a multinational group active in health data analytics and clinical research. The investigation concerned a database containing health information relating to approximately one million patients of 800 general practitioners, used for studies commissioned also by pharmaceutical companies. The investigation, which followed inspections carried out in April 2025, was joined with proceedings concerning a personal data breach notified by IQVIA.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA found that the data were not anonymous, as claimed by IQVIA. A persistent identifier assigned to each patient allowed individuals to be tracked over time and, combined with detailed information including year of birth, sex, diagnoses, symptoms, prescriptions, examinations, vaccinations and location data, made it possible to single out and potentially re-identify patients using reasonably available means.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA found that IQVIA, as controller, processed health data without an appropriate legal basis and without providing adequate information to patients. It also failed to establish appropriate retention periods, carry out a data protection impact assessment and implement adequate security measures. The database also contained directly identifying information relating to approximately 3 370 patients, including health data for approximately 3 080 of them.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA imposed an administrative fine of EUR 7 000 000 on IQVIA Solutions Italy S.r.l.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;If IQVIA intends to continue the processing, it must bring it into compliance with the GDPR within 120 days, including by identifying an appropriate legal basis, complying with its information obligations towards patients, carrying out a data protection impact assessment and appointing the general practitioners as processors. Alternatively, the anonymisation process must be carried out independently by the general practitioners in accordance with the safeguards specified by the Italian Authority.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In determining the amount of the fine, the Italian DPA took into account, among other factors, the large number of data subjects involved, the sensitive nature of the data, as well as mitigating factors including the suspension of data transfers by general practitioners and IQVIA’s cooperation during the proceedings.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10302141"&gt;COMUNICATO STAMPA - Dati sanitari: 7 milioni di euro di sanzione&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
    <dc:creator>EDPB</dc:creator>

  <title>Italian DPA fines security company EUR 39 000 for violations concerning employees’ data</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/italian-dpa-fines-security-company-eur-39-000-for-violations-concerning-employees-data_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 6 August 2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: La Patria S.p.A.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject), Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject) and Article 15 (Right to access by the data subject)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Key words: Data subjects rights, Fines&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) initiated an investigation following a complaint lodged by a former employee of La Patria S.p.A., a security and technological security company. The complainant claimed that the company had failed to respond to two requests to access documentation concerning disciplinary proceedings against him, including data collected through a GPS system installed on the company vehicle assigned to him. The employee had requested access to the documentation in order to defend himself in disciplinary proceedings which subsequently resulted in his dismissal.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Garante, the Italian DPA, found that the company had failed to adequately respond to the employee’s access requests. The DPA clarified that a data subject does not need to expressly refer to the GDPR for a request to qualify as an exercise of the right of access. Furthermore, where a controller decides not to comply with a request, it must inform the data subject of the reasons and of the possibility of lodging a complaint or seeking a judicial remedy..&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;They also found that the company had failed to provide employees with appropriate information on the processing of geolocation data collected through GPS systems installed on company vehicles. Such data constitute personal data because the vehicle’s location can be indirectly linked to the employee driving it.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In addition, the company’s privacy notices incorrectly referred to the processing of special categories of personal data, including information concerning philosophical beliefs and sex life, although the company did not actually process such data.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Garante imposed a total administrative fine of EUR 39 000 on La Patria S.p.A. for infringements of Articles 12, 13 and 15 GDPR. The total fine consisted of EUR 22 000 for the infringements concerning the exercise of the right of access and EUR17 000 EUR for the infringements concerning the information provided to employees.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;When determining the fine, the Italian DPA took into account, among other factors, that the company had taken steps during the proceedings to bring its processing activities into compliance with the GDPR. In particular, it provided employees with appropriate information concerning the processing of geolocation data and removed incorrect references to special categories of personal data from its privacy notice.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;No further corrective measures were imposed, as the infringements had ceased and the company had already taken measures to remedy the identified shortcomings.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10300466#2"&gt;Garante: sanzione di 39mila euro a società di vigilanza di Bologna&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>

  <title>Italian DPA fines Emirates EUR 180 000 for infringements concerning passengers’ health data</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/italian-dpa-fines-emirates-eur-180-000-for-infringements-concerning-passengers-health-data_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 14 May 2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: Emirates&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject) and Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Website topics: Health and research, Basic principles&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case &amp;nbsp;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) initiated an investigation following a complaint lodged by a passenger concerning the processing of health data by Emirates in connection with assistance for passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The complainant stated that Emirates had required her to complete a MEDIF (Medical Information for Fitness to Travel or Special Assistance) form, although she claimed not to fall within the categories of passengers required to do so. The form collected information concerning passengers’ health, as well as data relating to their doctor and any accompanying person. The complainant also raised concerns about the information provided regarding the processing of such data.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;After consulting the Italian Civil Aviation Authority, the Italian DPA found that the processing of health data through the MEDIF form could be lawful where necessary to ensure safe air transport and provide appropriate assistance to passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility. Therefore, it found no infringement of Articles 5(1)(a)-(c), 6(1) and 9 GDPR concerning the lawfulness of collecting such data.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;However, Emirates failed to provide sufficiently clear, complete and transparent information about the processing. Passengers could not easily determine in advance whether their condition required completion of the MEDIF form, or clearly identify relevant information such as the purposes, legal bases and retention periods.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA also found that the seven-year retention period applied to MEDIF data was excessive in relation to the purposes of assessing fitness to fly and providing assistance during the journey.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA imposed an administrative fine of EUR 180 000 on Emirates for infringements of Articles 5(1)(a), 5(1)(e), 12 and 13 GDPR.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA also ordered Emirates, within 30 days, to bring the processing into compliance. In particular, the company must clearly identify the categories of passengers required to complete the MEDIF form and specify which sections and fields are necessary. It must also establish appropriate retention periods for MEDIF data and delete data retained beyond the newly defined period.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In determining the fine, the Italian DPA took into account, among other factors, the limited number of passengers concerned compared with Emirates’ overall customer base, the absence of an intention to discriminate against the complainant, the corrective measures imposed and the absence of previous data protection infringements by the company.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/web/guest/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10259296"&gt;Decision concerning Emirates (IT)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>

<item>
  <title>Italian DPA fines BBVA EUR 5 508 000 for failing to respect a customer’s objection to direct marketing</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/italian-dpa-fines-bbva-eur-5-508-000-for-failing-to-respect-a-customers-objection-to-direct_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 3 July 2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A., Italian branch (BBVA)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject), Article 21 (Right to object), Article 24 (Responsibility of the controller)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Website topics: Basic principles, Data subjects rights, Marketing&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case &amp;nbsp;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) investigated BBVA, a multinational Spanish banking group, following a complaint from a customer who continued to receive promotional communications through the bank’s mobile app despite having objected to direct marketing.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The customer exercised his right to object through the settings provided in the BBVA app and subsequently reiterated his objection to the bank’s Customer Service. Nevertheless, promotional notifications continued for seven months, from October 2025 to May 2026.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;BBVA explained that the customer’s choice had been correctly recorded but that a technical failure prevented synchronisation between its internal systems and the Customer Relationship Management unit responsible for sending commercial communications.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA found that BBVA failed to give effect to the customer’s objection correctly and in a timely manner. During the relevant period, the customer received at least ten unsolicited commercial notifications.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The DPA rejected BBVA’s argument that the customer should have used the dedicated email addresses indicated in its privacy policy. The customer had correctly exercised his right through the app and had also contacted Customer Service. Controllers must facilitate the exercise of data subject rights and cannot disregard a valid request merely because it was not submitted through a preferred channel.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The DPA also found deficiencies in BBVA’s technical and organisational measures. In particular, Customer Service provided incorrect information by telling the customer that promotional pop-up notifications in the app could not be disabled, although BBVA subsequently demonstrated that they could be stopped.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Italian DPA found infringements of Articles 5(1)(a), 12, 21 and 24 GDPR and imposed an administrative fine of EUR 5 508 000.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The DPA ordered BBVA to adopt appropriate technical and organisational measures to facilitate the exercise of data subject rights and to ensure that requests are handled correctly and without undue delay. BBVA must also inform the DPA, within 30 days of notification of the decision, of the measures taken to comply with the order.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;When determining the fine, the DPA considered that the infringement concerned one data subject, lasted seven months and involved contact data for marketing purposes. It also considered BBVA’s remedial measures as a mitigating factor and a previous relevant infringement as an aggravating factor.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://gpdp.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10294220#1"&gt;Decision concerning Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. (IT)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
    <dc:creator>EDPB</dc:creator>
    <guid isPermaLink="false">a8ffc0a8-feab-474c-9193-7c4d4a52287e</guid>

<item>
  <title>Swedish DPA fines Miljödata i Karlskrona approximately EUR 160 000 for insufficient technical and organisational measures to ensure information security</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/swedish-dpa-fines-miljodata-i-karlskrona-approximately-eur-160-000-for-insufficient-technical_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 22/09/2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 32 (Security of processing)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Website topics: Cybersecurity, personal data breaches&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;In August 2025, the IT service provider Miljödata was targeted in a cyberattack, during which a malicious actor gained access to a large volume of personal data and subsequently published data on the darknet. According to the company, the incident affected 2.2 million individuals. Among Miljödata’s customers affected by the attack are a majority of Sweden’s municipalities, several regions, and government agencies, as well as a large number of private companies. The compromised data included personal identity numbers, contact details, and sensitive data related to sick leave, rehabilitation, and student-related incidents in schools.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The review shows that the company did not maintain a sufficiently high level of technical and organizational security, given the types of personal data it processed. Miljödata failed to conduct adequate checks when installing new software and did not have automated real-time monitoring of its systems to detect intrusions or suspicious activity.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;IMY, the Swedish Data Protection Authority, assesses that Miljödata acted negligently and has therefore decided to impose an administrative fine of SEK 1 800 000 (approximately EUR 160 000) for violating Article 32(1) GDPR.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.imy.se/en/news/administrative-fine-against-miljodata/"&gt;Administrative Fine against Miljödata&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>

  <title>Hellenic DPA decision on a data breach involving E.E.T.A.A. S.A. as processor for the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/hellenic-dpa-decision-on-a-data-breach-involving-eetaa-sa-as-processor-for-the-ministry-of_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 28/07/2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 25 (Data protection by design and by default), Article 28 (Processor), Article 32 (Security of processing), Article 33 (Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority) and Article 34 (Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order,&amp;nbsp;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case &amp;nbsp;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Hellenic Data Protection Authority (DPA) investigated a large-scale personal data breach affecting the information systems of the Hellenic Agency for Local Development and Local Government (E.E.T.A.A.) S.A., which were used to implement programmes of the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The breach affected databases containing personal data of a large number of data subjects, including identification and contact details, financial and health data. The Hellenic DPA found that the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs, in its capacity as controller, had complied with its obligations concerning the notification of the breach to the Authority and its communication to the affected data subjects. However, the Authority found that the success of the attack was associated with E.E.T.A.A.’s continued use of outdated information systems and inadequate security measures, despite its awareness of the relevant risks. The DPA found infringements of the requirements relating to the security of processing, as well as deficiencies in compliance with the requirements of Article 28 GDPR governing the relationship between the controller and the processor.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Hellenic DPA imposed administrative fines of EUR 200 000 on the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs and EUR 150 000 on E.E.T.A.A. It also ordered the parties (i.e. the Ministry and E.E.T.A.A.) to enter into a data processing agreement pursuant to Article 28 GDPR and to fully implement the planned measures to strengthen the security of their information systems.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.dpa.gr/el/enimerwtiko/prakseisArxis/apofasi-gia-peristatiko-parabiasis-prosopikon-dedomenon-eetaa-me-tin"&gt;Decision on an incident of personal data breach of EETAA in his capacity as a processor on behalf of the data controller of YKOISO (EL)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>

  <title>Dutch DPA fines Uber EUR 824 990 000 for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information on profiling</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/dutch-dpa-fines-uber-eur-824-990-000-for-unlawful-automated-decision-making-and-insufficient_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Cross-border case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Controller: Uber B.V&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 22 (Automated individual decision making, including profiling) and Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Key words: Automated decision making, profiling and online tracking, fines&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), the Dutch data protection authority, imposes a fine of EUR 824 990 000 on Uber. The reason for this is that the AP has ruled that Uber made fully automated decisions about drivers. In case of suspicions of fraud or customer reviews that were too low, drivers' accounts were automatically temporarily deactivated or, in case of persistent low customer reviews, permanently deactivated. As a result, their income was lost via Uber during the deactivation.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Complaints from 171 French Uber drivers, submitted through the Ligue des droits de l’Homme (LDH) to the French Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL), led to the investigation. As Uber’s European headquarters are in the Netherlands, the case was handled by the Dutch data protection authority, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), under the GDPR One-Stop-Shop procedure. The case concerned incidents between 2018 and 2022.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;According to the AP, Uber has violated the prohibition of fully automated decision-making under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The AP also found that Uber did not sufficiently inform drivers about automatic decision-making. Uber has now stopped the violations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;At the moment, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) imposed an administrative fine of EUR 824 990 000 on Uber for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information about profiling. Uber has appealed the fine, and there is no final judicial decision yet.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://Uber fined nearly 825 million euros for automated driver blocking"&gt;Uber fined nearly 825 million euros for automated driver blocking&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
  <pubDate>Thu, 08 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
    <dc:creator>EDPB</dc:creator>
    <guid isPermaLink="false">b7ce37b6-62ea-41f8-a4e6-5d7fb6620d40</guid>

    <category>Automated decision making, profiling and Online tracking</category>

  <title>The Irish Data Protection Commission fines Google EUR 403 000 000 following Inquiry into Google’s processing of location data</title>
  <link>https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/the-irish-data-protection-commission-fines-google-403-000-000-eur-following-inquiry_en</link>
  <description>&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="background-information"&gt;Background information&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Date of final decision: 21 September 2026&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;National case&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 6 (Lawfulness of processing), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject) and Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject)&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Decision: Administrative fine, compliance order&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Key words: GDPR enforcement, technology, accountability, data subjects rights&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="heading-wrapper"&gt;&lt;h2 id="summary-of-the-decision"&gt;Summary of the Decision&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Origin of the case &amp;nbsp;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) has announced its final decision following an inquiry into Google Ireland Limited (Google). This own-volition Inquiry was launched by the DPC, in its role as the Lead Supervisory Authority for Google, in February 2020, following receipt of complaints from several European consumer rights organisations, including BEUC, regarding Google’s processing of location data in connection with certain services and products.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The scope of the Inquiry concerned Google’s processing of location data in three specific features – “Web &amp;amp; App Activity”, “Location History” and “Location Accuracy” between the date of application of the GDPR, 25 May 2018 to 4 February 2020.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Findings&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The decision, which was made by the Commissioners for Data Protection, finds that Google infringed the GDPR in respect of:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;the lawfulness and fairness of its processing of location data in Web &amp;amp; App Activity and Location History;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;its accountability obligations under the GDPR by failing to be able to demonstrate compliance with the lawfulness, fairness and transparency principle regarding its processing of personal data in Location Accuracy;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;its transparency obligations in respect of all three features referred to above; and&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;its retention of location data in Web &amp;amp; App Activity and Location History.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Decision&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The DPC has imposed administrative fines totalling EUR 403 000 000 and has ordered Google to bring its processing into compliance within 6 months.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For further information:&lt;/strong&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://dataprotection.ie/en/news-media/latest-news/data-protection-commission-fines-google-eu403-million-following-inquiry-googles-processing-location"&gt;Data Protection Commission fines Google €403 million following inquiry into Google’s processing of location data&amp;nbsp;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</description>
